title: Impairment of an individual asset: Verma's machine (lecture exercise 3.1)
text: At the end of N Verma tests a machine for impairment. Carrying amount: €200,000; remaining useful life: 5 years. Fair value (less costs to sell) at the end of N: €150,000.
Expected cash flows: €40,000 at the end of each of the next five years; discount rate 8%; annuity factor (8%, 5 years) = 3.993.

title: Company Beta – impairment of two CGUs (exam 2024)
text: Company Beta consists of two cash-generating units, A and B. The land and building of CGU A and the building of CGU B are in sectors with a drop in property prices, so an impairment test must be carried out for them. In addition, IAS 36 requires an impairment test for all CGUs (they contain goodwill) at the end of year N.

title: PRODI – bank loan or lease? (exam 2024)
text: The CFO of PRODI considers two ways to finance a new production line worth €1,000,000, used for 10 years and commissioned on 2 January N. PRODI already has a high gearing ratio, so the CFO thinks a lease contract would be better.
Solution 1 – bank loan of €1,000,000: repayment in fine after 10 years, interest rate 4.65%.

Solution 2 – lease contract: annual rent €128,000 payable on 31/12 (first rent 31/12/N, 10 rents), duration 10 years, effective interest rate 4.76%, fair value of the line €1,000,000 (= present value of all lease payments).

title: Adams Corporation – lessee accounting (lecture exercise 3.5)
text: On 1 January N1 Adams signed a 4-year non-cancellable lease for a specific machine, which it can use according to its production needs. Payments: $9,968 at the beginning of N1 and four further payments of $9,968 at the end of N1, N2, N3, N4. Useful life of the machine: 6 years; straight-line depreciation; interest rate of the contract 10%; annuity factor (10%, 4 years) = 3.169865.

title: Ramon Inc. – impairment of a shopping mall under the cost model (exam 2019)
text: On 1 January N1 Ramon spent 300 million € to acquire a shopping mall for renting, depreciated straight-line over 30 years (cost model). On 31 December N5 shopping property prices have fallen sharply.
Estimated selling price on 31 December N5: 210 million €. Annual rent (paid on 31 December): 24 million €. Discount rate 10%. Residual value at the end of N30: zero.
Discount factors at 10% for an annual amount: 30 years 9.42 · 25 years 9.08 · 24 years 8.98 · 20 years 8.51.

title: Malaga – industrial machine (lecture case)
text: Malaga (IFRS, listed) received an industrial machine on 1 October N; it was ready to use on 31 October N.
Purchase price excl. tax USD 600,000 (1 USD = 0.9 EUR on the purchase date). Transport €26,000. Installation by Malaga's own workers €5,000. User training by the constructor €10,000.
Depreciation is based on units produced: N 50,000 · N+1 150,000 · N+2 200,000 · N+3 100,000 units. Residual value (resale price) at the end: €200,000.
From 15 to 20 January N+2, modifications of €40,000 increase the production capacity. Production is now planned at 250,000 units in N+2 and 110,000 in N+3.

title: Malaga – building with a new roof (lecture case)
text: In January N Malaga bought a new building for industrial use for €6,000,000. The useful life of the building is 30 years, but a new roof is planned after 15 years; the estimated cost of the new roof is €1,000,000. Straight-line depreciation, no residual value.

title: Malaga – patent with deferred payments (lecture case)
text: In January N Malaga acquired a patent: initial payment €30,000, followed by an annual licence fee of €10,000 for 10 years, payable at the end of each year. The discount rate usually applied by the company is 8%. The patent is amortised straight-line over 10 years.
Annuity factor at 8% for 10 years: 6.7101.

title: Bilbao – impairment of an airplane (lecture case)
text: In January N1 Bilbao acquired an airplane for €250 million, depreciated straight-line over 25 years (cost model).
On 31 December N5 airplane prices have fallen tremendously. The estimated selling price (net of costs to sell) is €180 million; a value in use above this amount cannot be demonstrated.

title: The goodwill of SEAT in the VW group (lecture case)
text: VW acquired SEAT for 5,000 MU; the goodwill was 500 MU and has never been impaired. SEAT is an operating segment and a CGU; its assets only generate cash flows together.
Expected free cash flows before interest and taxes (MU): x2 750 · x3 700 · x4 650 · x5 590 · x6 and following years 540 (constant perpetuity). WACC 11%.
BMW offers 5,100 MU for SEAT's net operating assets until 31 December x1; VW would incur transaction costs of 350 MU.
Net operating assets of SEAT at 31 December x1: property 1,250 · plant and equipment 2,500 · goodwill 500 · finished goods 700 · receivables 950 · payables (400) = 5,500.

title: Porto – impairment of three CGUs (lecture case)
text: Porto consists of three CGUs (A, B, C), each with allocated goodwill from 100%-owned acquisitions. The building of CGU B is in a sector with falling property prices; it has not been tested individually and its value in use cannot be determined on its own. IAS 36 requires an annual test of all CGUs (they contain goodwill).

title: RENT – lease of an office building (lecture case)
text: On 1 January N1 RENT enters into a lease of an office building for its own use (useful life of the building 40 years, straight-line).

Lease payments: €300,000 per year. The first payment is made on 1 January N1; the following payments are made on 31 December of each year, the last one on 31 December N12. RENT's incremental borrowing rate is 4.5%.
Annuity factor at 4.5% for 12 years: 9.1186.

title: Burger Queen – scooters and a building (lecture case)
text: On 1 January N1 the restaurant chain Burger Queen (BQ) enters into two leases (straight-line depreciation):
A) Delivery scooters: €10,000 per year at the end of each year for 5 years; incremental borrowing rate 4% (annuity factor 4.4518).

B) Building in Paris: 10-year lease with an option to extend by 5 years that BQ is NOT reasonably certain to exercise. Payments €50,000 at the end of each year. Initial direct costs €20,000, of which the owner reimburses the €5,000 real estate commission as an incentive. Incremental borrowing rate 5% (annuity factor 10 years 7.7217).
